title: tekton famspec -- a structured request to GENERATE one family (.rfa)
description: A famspec is the `rfa` INPUT of the permutation router (tools/route.py run --rfa FAMSPEC.json | '{...inline...}'): a request to generate ONE Revit family from catalog facts with tekton's own constructors (rvt.famgen.factory.make_panelboard / make_transformer / make_luminaire / make_device; rvt.ifc.famfrom_ifc.make_downlight), never a copied family. `kind` selects the constructor; every other field mirrors that constructor's keyword arguments and is optional (the constructor's default applies). `--output rfa` delivers the standalone .rfa (family-mode validator + provenance scan in the manifest); `--output rvt` additionally LOADS it into a host project (default: the pinned certified genesis base; `--rvt yours.rvt` for your own) through the four-registry loader. Facts the catalog does not carry are refused BY NAME in one clear line, never invented. Every output is stamped PROOF-ONLY until the deliverability gates clear -- delivered regardless.

common.description: Fields every kind accepts (documentation only; each kind lists them explicitly because draft-07 additionalProperties does not see through $ref).

name.description: Family name override (default: composed from the facts, e.g. 'Panelboard 480Y/277 400A MCB 42ckt Surface').

solid.description: true (default) = author the enclosure/housing solid at the catalog dimensions; false = the parametric skeleton without the solid (a diagnostic sibling).

target_version.description: The recipient's Revit year. Same meaning as route.py --target-version (the CLI flag wins when both are given): 2026/2025/2024 emit the .rfa AS that release; an uncertified or unknown year is delivered at the default release with THE one line saying which Revit opens it. Revit cannot open a newer file -- ask the recipient's year.

shared_params.description: Path to OUR shared-parameter TXT (or the word 'default' = usecases/eaton-panelboard/panelboard-shared-parameters.txt): every parameter it names is authored SHARED at that file's GUID so schedules/tags bind by GUID; omitted = every parameter local.

standards.description: Author the CATEGORY STANDARD PARAMETERS (rvt.famgen.standards): the parameters a family of this category/product is expected to carry -- a data device gets Device Type / Mounting / Mounting Height / Number of Ports / Cable Category ..., a lighting fixture its photometrics, a mechanical equipment its airflow and MCA/MOCP. Default true. Every parameter's spec and group id is verified against the units table the format itself ships; the NAMES of the convention-sourced ones are INFERRED and the report says which. A parameter the constructor already authored is left exactly as it was. A category with no table yet is reported as an honest gap, never a silent bare family.

standard_values.description: Values for the standard parameters, by parameter NAME, in internal units (feet for lengths). Supply only the ones actually known -- every other standard parameter is authored BLANK, which is the honest state of a fact nobody supplied. A name matching no standard parameter of the category comes back in the report as 'values_not_placed'.

typeSelector.description: One family TYPE (type-table row): a rating along the product's axis (mains A / kVA / W) as a number or a '225A' / '45kVA' / '38W' string, or an object over the kind's per-type fields plus an optional explicit 'type_name'.

types.description: MULTI-TYPE family: one type-table row per selector; the first is the primary type (the one authored solid is built at its dimensions). Omitted = the single type the scalar fields describe.

voltage.description: A system voltage: '480Y/277', '208Y/120', '120-277', or a bare line voltage number (480).

vendor.description: Catalog vendor key (facts on file today: 'eaton', 'square-d'); anything else is refused by name.

line.description: Product line key ('pow-r-line' / 'prl' for eaton; 'nq' / 'nf' for square-d).

mains_a.description: Mains rating in amperes (default 400); must sit on the member's tabulated sizing rows.

mcb.description: true = main circuit breaker (default), false = main lugs only.

panel_name.description: PanelName parameter value (the schedule tag, e.g. 'DP-7'); default 'PANEL'.

sccr_ka.description: Short-circuit current rating in kA; omitted = the low end of the member's fully-rated range for the voltage (a fact), flagged as such.

kva.description: Rating in kVA (default 75); a rating whose dimensions the catalog does not publish is refused by name.

vendor.description: Catalog vendor key (facts on file today: 'eaton', 'hps').

fixture.description: The luminaire archetype = make_luminaire's own `kind` argument, renamed here because `kind` selects the constructor: 'recessed-troffer' (default) / 'troffer', or 'recessed-downlight' / 'downlight' (OUR parametric can).

aperture_in.description: Downlight aperture in inches (OUR parametric value, flagged 'given').

device.title: kind = device -> rvt.famgen.factory.make_device(kind=device, **fields): a WIRING DEVICE family (category Electrical Fixtures, OST -2001060)
device.description: A duplex receptacle (NEMA 5-15R / 5-20R), a single-pole switch or a 4 in square junction box from the `generic/devices-and-mounting` facts: faceplate proud of the family XY plane (the wall face of a work-plane-based family; no face-hosting claim) + the device box recessed behind it, ONE 1-pole primary power connector bound to the `Voltage` / `Apparent Load` parameters, `Mounting Height` from the facts. One type per family (no `types` list): the envelope figures are 'assumed' on the record and surface as such in the report.

The wiring device = make_device's own `kind` argument, renamed here because `kind` selects the constructor (rvt.famgen.factory.DEVICE_KINDS): 'duplex-receptacle' (default, NEMA 5-15R), 'duplex-receptacle-20a' (NEMA 5-20R), 'switch' (single-pole toggle), 'junction-box' (4 in square).

mounting_height_in.description: Height above the finished floor in inches ('given'); omitted = the record's convention (18 in receptacles / junction boxes, 48 in switches, 'assumed') inside the ADA 15..48 in reach range, which is the sourced FACT.

va.description: Booked connector load in volt-amperes (default 180 = the NEC 220.14(I) receptacle unit load; 0 for a switch / junction box that books none).

downlight.title: kind = downlight -> rvt.ifc.famfrom_ifc.make_downlight(**fields): the MEASURED product archetype (facts read from a product IFC)
downlight.description: This lane emits on the family container archetype, which lives in the git-ignored research corpus: it runs on the owner machine only until famfrom_ifc emits on the bundled base (a fresh clone answers with one clear line). The catalog kinds (panelboard / transformer / luminaire / device) run anywhere.

ifc_path.description: The product IFC to measure (default: inputs/ifc/chicago-plenum-downlight.ifc).

photometric_web.description: IES reference (a URL/file NAME parameter value; no photometric file is bundled).

detail.description: 'standard' = can + trim + lens + frame + boxes + hangers; 'envelope' = can + trim ring only.

archetype.title: kind = archetype -> rvt.famgen.factory.make_archetype(**fields): a NAMED PRODUCT generated at standard NOMINAL sizes
archetype.description: Neither catalog-backed nor caller-supplied geometry: name a product this engine generates ('cable_tray', 'strut_channel', 'wireway', 'junction_box', 'conduit') and it is built at the standard nominal sizes for that product CLASS, LOD 400 -- a ladder tray is two side rails plus rungs at the standard spacing, not a box with a label. EVERY dimension is reported: 'nominal' (generated by the archetype from standard practice, listed in the report's unverified_fields, NEVER a manufacturer claim -- no manufacturer, model or part number is attached) or 'given' (you stated it, in 'dimensions' or in 'prompt'). Claiming a manufacturer's part is still refused, because that is a fact the catalog would have to hold. `python -m rvt.famgen.archetypes` prints every product, its parameters and the practice each nominal follows.

product.description: The generated product: 'cable_tray' (ladder), 'strut_channel', 'wireway', 'junction_box', 'conduit'. An unknown name is refused BY NAME and lists what is generated -- nothing is invented from a name alone.

dimensions.description: Override any of the archetype's parameters BY NAME, in that parameter's own unit (e.g. {"width_in": 24, "length_ft": 20, "rung_spacing_in": 6}). Every key you set is reported 'given'; everything else stays 'nominal'. An unknown parameter name is refused by name.

prompt.description: Optional free text read for any dimension 'dimensions' did not set ('a 24 inch cable tray 20 ft long with 6 in rung spacing'). Anything it states becomes 'given', with the words quoted back in the report.

category.description: Family category override; each archetype already declares the right one (a ladder tray goes to Cable Tray Fittings, a junction box to Electrical Fixtures). The category also selects the standard parameter set.

base_z_ft.description: Base elevation of the product in the family (default 0).

generic_model.title: kind = generic_model -> rvt.famgen.factory.make_generic_model(**fields): an ARBITRARY 3D object, geometry GIVEN by the caller
generic_model.description: NOT catalog-backed: the caller supplies the geometry (a Claude Design body, an IFC solid, a measured object, or a model's own decomposition of 'a bus') and every dimension is flagged GIVEN with its source in the report -- never presented as a manufacturer fact. ONE solid: 'vertices' (a closed planar ring in feet) or 'width_ft' + 'depth_ft', extruded 'height_ft'. MANY solids: 'parts', which is how an arbitrary object is expressed -- each part is its own prism placed in the family's frame, so a bus is a body plus wheels plus windows rather than one block. 'height_ft' is required for the single-solid form; with 'parts' it is each part that carries its own height.

vertices.description: Closed planar ring in the family plane, feet: [[x, y], ...]. Mutually exclusive with width_ft/depth_ft.

base_z_ft.description: Base elevation of the extrusion in the family (default 0).

category.description: Family category (default 'generic_model'; e.g. 'furniture', 'electrical_equipment', 'data_devices'). The category also selects the STANDARD PARAMETER SET the family carries -- see 'standards'.

standards.description: Author the CATEGORY STANDARD PARAMETERS (rvt.famgen.standards): the parameters a family of this category is expected to carry -- a data device gets Device Type / Mounting / Mounting Height / Number of Ports / Cable Category ..., a lighting fixture gets its photometrics, a mechanical equipment its airflow and MCA/MOCP. Default true. Every parameter's spec and group id is verified against the units table the format itself ships; the NAMES of the convention-sourced ones are INFERRED, and the report says which. A category with no table yet is reported as an honest gap, never a silent bare family.

standard_values.description: Values for the category's standard parameters, by parameter NAME, in internal units (feet for lengths). Supply only the ones actually known -- every other standard parameter is authored BLANK, which is the honest state of a fact nobody supplied. A name matching no standard parameter of the category comes back in the report as 'values_not_placed'.

source.description: Where the geometry came from, recorded on every GIVEN dimension (e.g. 'claude-design', 'ifc:body').

parts.description: The object as a list of SOLIDS, each authored in the family's frame (feet). This is the general form: anything that can be described as prisms -- a cable tray's rails and rungs, a bus's body, wheels and windows -- is expressible here without a catalog entry, an IFC or a donor. Overall Width/Depth/Height parameters report the assembly's bounding box. When 'parts' is given, the single-solid fields (height_ft / vertices / width_ft / depth_ft) are ignored.

shape.description: PRISMS authored directly: box = width_ft x depth_ft; cylinder = radius_ft (or diameter_ft) about the VERTICAL axis; polygon = vertices, a closed ring, convex or concave. cylinder_x / cylinder_y = a TRUE cylinder lying along X or Y -- a WHEEL, an axle, a pipe run -- from radius_ft + length_ft; its vertical extent is the diameter, so it needs no height_ft. STACKED approximations, still sliced because the part contract extrudes along Z: sphere and dome = radius_ft; cone = radius_ft + height_ft (+ optional top_radius_ft for a frustum). A stack reports its authored-vs-true volume ratio and 'segments' tunes it; the true cylinders do not need it.

height_ft.description: Extrusion height in feet (the part's Z extent).

base_z_ft.description: Base elevation of this part in the family (default 0), so parts STACK into a real object instead of one blob.

center.description: Plan centre [x, y] in feet (box / cylinder). A polygon's ring already carries its position; center offsets it.

diameter_ft.description: cylinder only; an alternative to radius_ft.

vertices.description: polygon only: a closed planar ring in feet, any winding.

name.description: What this part IS ('body', 'front wheel left', 'rung 3'). Carried into the family so the object reads as its parts.

length_ft.description: cylinder_x / cylinder_y only: the length ALONG the horizontal axis.

top_radius_ft.description: cone only: a non-zero value makes it a frustum (0 = a true cone tip).

segments.description: Slices a STACKED round body (sphere / dome / cone) is built from: default 16, capped at 64. Higher = closer to the true body and MORE SOLIDS; the report carries the authored/true volume ratio so the trade is measured. Ignored by cylinder_x / cylinder_y, which are real cylinders rather than stacks.

items.description: One solid. 'height_ft' is required for box / cylinder / polygon and for cone; sphere / dome / cylinder_x / cylinder_y derive their extent from radius_ft (and length_ft).
